title: Metropolitan Police Detective Love Story 4
notes: case_type: robbery (no homicide victim); `label.murderer_id` is used per this dataset's generic convention to hold the culprit id (the robber), not a literal murderer. The old wiki-summary file (cases/ep253-254_metropolitan_police_detective_love_story_4.json) omitted the detective-cast romance A-plot entirely (Takagi/Sato/Shiratori arranged-marriage subplot that structures the whole episode's stakes and timeline) and modeled only the robbery puzzle with three bare suspect nodes and no locations besides the store. Its culprit identification (Yasuo Kamieda / Kamieda Yasuo, the school coach) is CONFIRMED correct against the full two-part transcript, so `label.murderer_id` is unchanged in substance. This rebuild adds: the full detective-cast relationship network (Takagi-Sato mutual romantic interest, Sato-Shiratori arranged-marriage candidacy, employer/butler/family ties), the sunset-deadline ultimatum that drives the episode, six distinct locations instead of one, concrete objects (the discarded disguise, the knife, Mamehara's photochromic glasses, Kamieda's wristwatch, Koshimizu's two wristwatches) instead of a single vague object description, and `was_at` opportunity edges for every one of the three suspects (not just the culprit) plus the three witnesses, grounded directly in the transcript's restroom-detention and witness-relocation scenes. No interpersonal motive network applies (impersonal robbery, not a targeted crime), so no `has_motive_against` edges are generated, consistent with the old file's own note on this point; Kamieda's financial motive (divorce settlement money) is instead recorded in his `attrs`.

clues.desc: The elderly witness's testimony (a taller woman in blue) reconciles once you factor in his generation's habit of calling green 'blue' (explaining the color) and his misreading of a wristwatch worn face-inward toward the wrist as a feminine style (explaining the perceived gender) -- both point to Kamieda, not a woman.

Mamehara's testimony (black shirt, ~170cm) reconciles once you factor in his not-yet-adjusted photochromic glasses, which tinted the robber's true green shirt black in his memory, while his height estimate of 170cm was accurate all along.

The clothing-store witness's testimony (male, ~180cm, green shirt) reconciles once you factor in the robber running along the raised sidewalk curb to avoid the crowd, which exaggerated his apparent height from a true 170cm, while her color report (green) and gender read were accurate.
